idiom_name: System.Text.Json source-generated JsonSerializerContext plus JsonSchema.Net validation (or Google.Protobuf codegen)
implementation_notes: The platform serializer carries the binding: [JsonSerializable(typeof(Order))] on a partial JsonSerializerContext makes the source generator emit reader/writer code, JsonSerializerOptions.PropertyNamingPolicy fixes the wire naming convention, and JsonSchema.Net validates incoming payloads against the published JSON Schema (JsonSchema.FromText(schema).Evaluate(element)). When the contract is IDL-first, protoc --csharp_out (Google.Protobuf) generates message classes instead, exactly as on the other runtimes; XSD-first seams still bind through System.Xml.Serialization attributes. The reflection-based POCO form remains valid for internal seams, but AOT/trimmed deployments need the generated context anyway.
pitfalls: Reflection-based serialisation is removed by trimming and Native AOT: without the source-generated context (or an explicit TypeInfoResolver) the failure appears at runtime, not at build time.
Deserialisation ignores unknown members while reserialisation drops them silently: unknown-field preservation requires JsonExtensionData or JsonUnmappedMemberHandling to be configured deliberately.
Casing and enum representation are contract decisions: changing JsonNamingPolicy or adding a JsonStringEnumConverter rewrites the wire format for every participant.
